title: Your week has a genre. Which one is it?
dek: Twelve questions about how the last seven days actually went, and the era your life is currently stuck in.

questions.prompt: Your week gets a title card. It reads:

options.label: AND THEN EVERYTHING HAPPENED AT ONCE

questions.prompt: The last photo in your camera roll is a screenshot of a message you didn't reply to.

options.label: Reply now, three days late, no apology
Send it to the group chat as a joke
Read it again and decide tomorrow

questions.prompt: The week comes with a soundtrack. Pick one:

options.label: One long ambient track, no vocals

questions.prompt: Drop the dot. Where does this month's version of you actually live?
questions.helper: Left to right is billing. Bottom to top is behaviour. You can be both.

questions.prompt: I rehearse a conversation and then never have it.
questions.high: I've had it four times in my head

questions.prompt: A stranger asks what you do. There's a version of the answer you only use at parties.

options.label: The polished one, with a joke at the end
The true one, including the mess
The one that makes you sound dangerous

questions.prompt: I'd rather be interesting than comfortable.
Pick the street you'd take the long way home down.

options.label: Cobbles, old shopfronts, no one around
options.alt: A cobbled street of old shopfronts

options.label: A crossing, traffic, somewhere to be
options.alt: A city crossing with traffic and pedestrians

options.label: Neon, late, slightly too loud
options.alt: A street at night lit by neon signs

questions.prompt: The thing you were dreading is cancelled.
I've described my week as a 'plot point' out loud.
A good entrance is worth being late for.
The week ends and nobody claps.

options.label: Text the group: was that weird?

results.name: Main Character
results.tagline: The plot is briefly about you
results.blurb: This week you're the one things happen to. You're making decisions out loud, wearing the outfit, taking the call in the street. It's not vanity — it's momentum, and it's contagious. Just remember the people in your scenes are also main characters somewhere.
strengths: Turns an ordinary Tuesday into a story
Decides before the doubt catches up
Brings other people along
results.watchOut: Not every silence is a reaction to you. Let someone else have the monologue.

results.name: Soft Launch
results.blurb: You're in the phase where everything is 80% done and none of it is public. The draft, the new thing, the haircut. You're protecting it until it's good, which is sensible — and also a very comfortable place to hide indefinitely.
strengths: Protects work until it's ready
Notices what needs another pass
Low drama, high standards
results.watchOut: The last twenty percent can take a year. Show one person the rough version.

results.name: Villain Arc
results.blurb: You've stopped apologising for wanting things. This week has teeth: the boundary, the email you sent, the gym at 6am. People are calling it a phase. You're calling it a correction. Both can be true, but only one of them is going to change your life.
strengths: Uses anger as information
Sets a boundary and holds it
Doesn't need to be liked to continue
results.watchOut: The arc works better with an exit. Decide what would count as enough.

results.name: Golden Hour
results.blurb: This is the week where the light is good, the plans happen and nothing hurts too much. You're not naive about it — you can see the edges — you're just choosing to enjoy the middle of it. That's not luck. That's a skill.
strengths: Finds the good hour inside a bad day
Makes ordinary things feel like an occasion
Enjoys things while they're happening
results.watchOut: Don't spend the good part bracing for the end. It's already happening. Be in it.

results.name: Side Quest
results.tagline: The detour is the actual plot
results.blurb: You came for one thing and left with three others. You take the long route, talk to the stranger, follow the sign. None of it is on the plan and all of it is the good part. Your life is a series of excellent distractions.
strengths: Says yes to the unplanned thing
Finds the interesting person in any room
Keeps momentum when the plan collapses
results.watchOut: At some point the detour needs a destination. Finish one of them.

results.name: Lore Drop
results.blurb: You've been telling the story. The full one, with the timeline and the bit about your mother. It's how you process, and it's also how you find your people — the ones who lean in instead of backing away. You're not oversharing, you're filtering.
strengths: Turns experience into a good story
Connects fast and honestly
Gives other people permission to be real
results.watchOut: Some things need to stay yours for a while. Not everything is a chapter yet.

results.name: Deleted Scene
results.blurb: Something real happened this week and you've decided not to include it. Maybe it was embarrassing, maybe it was sad, maybe it was the best night of the month. Either way you're carrying a scene nobody else has seen, and it's taking up more room than you'd admit.
strengths: Keeps a private self intact
Doesn't perform every feeling
Notices what others leave out
results.watchOut: A secret gets heavier in the dark. Tell one safe person the short version.

results.name: Post-Credits Scene
results.blurb: You're the last one awake, after the party, after the group chat, after the year everyone else has moved on from. You're not lonely exactly — you're processing. The quiet bit at the end is where you actually figure out what the week meant.
strengths: Comfortable with the quiet aftermath
Sees the pattern once the noise stops
Doesn't need an audience to continue
results.watchOut: Don't stay in the empty cinema too long. The next film is already starting.

results.name: The Bottle Episode
results.tagline: One room, two people, no exits
results.blurb: Your week compresses into a single conversation in a single room, and everything gets said in it. No montage, no soundtrack, no cutaway — just the thing you've both been avoiding since spring. It's the cheapest episode of the season and the one everyone quotes.
strengths: Stays in the difficult conversation
Says the unsaid thing eventually
Needs no budget to be memorable
results.watchOut: Not every silence needs resolving tonight. Sleep on the second half.

results.name: The Flashback Episode
results.tagline: Everything is explained by one summer
results.blurb: Your month keeps cutting back to a year you thought was finished. A song in a shop, a photo in a drawer, and suddenly you're nineteen again with worse decisions. The present is fine; the past is just louder, and it's doing the voiceover.
strengths: Learns from what actually happened
Keeps the good bits intact
Connects the dots other people miss
results.watchOut: Nostalgia is a rerun. Do something in the current timeline.
